decision: One append-only, per-tenant `actor_event` tenant table (migration 018) is the SoD substrate: an ordinary T-0013 tenant table (tenant_id NOT NULL leading PK, FORCE RLS, default-DENY on choros.tenant_id GUC, choros_app NOBYPASSRLS, withTenant access) that records, per object, the closed verb trail {request,prepare,submit,approve,release}. Six structural decisions: (1) Append-only by the SAME dual mechanism as T-0016 audit_event — choros_app GRANT SELECT,INSERT ONLY (no UPDATE/DELETE) AND a BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE no-mutate trigger that RAISEs for ALL roles including the owner choros_migrator, so a privilege misconfig still fails closed; defeating append-only needs a CI-visible grant+trigger diff. (2) Per-tenant strictly-increasing seq with UNIQUE(tenant_id,seq) and PK(tenant_id,seq), assigned under a per-tenant counter row actor_event_seq(tenant_id PK, next_seq bigint) locked SELECT ... FOR UPDATE — NEVER a global SEQUENCE or global advisory lock; seq is sparse-tolerant (strictly increasing, density NOT required — distinct from T-0016's dense chain). (3) Actor identity splits performer from principal: actor (=performed_by) uuid NOT NULL FK (tenant_id,actor)->employee(tenant_id,id); on_behalf_of uuid NULL FK->employee (NULL ⇒ own behalf); SoD attributes to the principal = COALESCE(on_behalf_of, actor); role_at_event uuid NOT NULL point-in-time role_id carrying NO FK (deferred to T-0022, mirrors grant.role_id); kind∈{human,agent} is NOT a column of and NOT a discriminator in actor_event (equal actors — resolvable by joining employee). (4) object_ref is a denormalized opaque ResourceRef à la object_handle (T-0015): object_kind text NOT NULL CHECK IN ('application','registry','record') + nullable application_id/registry_id/record_id, NONE FK-enforced; object-scoped lookup is the primary indexed read path via INDEX(tenant_id, object_kind, record_id, registry_id, application_id, seq). (5) Verb vocabulary is closed-but-vocab-versioned: event text NOT NULL CHECK IN the five verbs (not an open string); approve_Ln modelled as event='approve' + approve_level smallint with CHECK ((event='approve') = (approve_level IS NOT NULL)) AND CHECK (approve_level IS NULL OR approve_level >= 1) so L1<L2<.. are orderable without N verb strings; vocab_version smallint NOT NULL pins the verb set + level semantics per row; extending the set is a CHECK edit + vocab bump migration, never a runtime string. (6) References-not-values: NO data/snapshot/view/payload column; only object_ref + identities; a single detail jsonb NULL is event metadata (no object field values); the gateway (T-0021) stays the sole object-value resolver. The ledger is intentionally NOT the audit floor: NO prev_hash/row_hash/chain columns, NO head table, and NO FK between actor_event and audit_event (each independently append-only); a guarded transition writes one actor_event row AND one audit_event row in distinct tables, optionally cross-referenced by the stable actor_event.id (UNIQUE(tenant_id,id)) — coupling is the writer's job (T-0021/E4.2). Design + DDL only: the migration emits the table, the per-tenant counter, triggers, grants, indexes, and the additive known_tenant_tables.txt entry; the writer (appendActorEvent) and SoD read queries are frozen as contracts (§4.3/§4.4), implemented by coder per this ADR and consumed by T-0032.

rejected_alternatives.option: Reuse T-0016's audit_head FOR-UPDATE row as the seq serialization point (or add an actor_event_head)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A head row is a head snapshot — the exact construct AC-21 forbids on this ledger (no head, no chain). T-0016's head exists to carry the chain head (seq,row_hash); actor_event has no chain so a head would be dead weight carrying only a counter. A dedicated single-column counter row (actor_event_seq, no row_hash, no chain semantics) gives per-tenant FOR-UPDATE serialization WITHOUT being a head/chain artefact, satisfying AC-21 while preserving T-0016's race-free pattern.

rejected_alternatives.option: Per-tenant advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(tenant_id))) as the seq primitive — no extra table
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Viable and table-free, but advisory-lock keys share one global int8 space, so a hashtext collision reintroduces cross-tenant contention (a soft NF-2 violation invisible until it bites) — the precise reason T-0016 rejected advisory locks. It is also a second source of truth for the counter (skew) separate from the rows we read anyway, and the lock is session/txn-scoped (no durable cursor). The counter row collapses serialization + the next-seq read into one FOR UPDATE op keyed exactly on tenant_id (no shared hash space). Acceptable-but-rejected; if the counter row is later judged heavy, an advisory lock keyed on the full tenant uuid (not a 32-bit hash) is the fallback — but day-1 = counter row.

rejected_alternatives.option: Global Postgres SEQUENCE (or one global advisory lock) feeding actor_event.seq
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Couples every tenant's write throughput onto one contention point (violates NF-2 per-tenant zero-contention) and makes seq tenant-global not tenant-scoped, breaking UNIQUE(tenant_id,seq) independence and the 'tenants order independently' guarantee (AC-8). Caught by ci/checks/actor_event_no_global_seq.sh + the AC-9 concurrency probe.

T-0016 needs density because its delete/gap defect signal is 'a missing seq = a deleted row'. actor_event has NO chain and NO gap-as-tamper semantics — SoD reasons over content and RELATIVE order (submit before approve), for which strictly-increasing is sufficient and density is gold-plating that would force a tighter serialization contract than SoD needs. FR-5 explicitly permits sparse. The invariant kept: per-tenant, strictly increasing, no global serialization.

rejected_alternatives.option: Hash-chain / head-snapshot the actor_event ledger for tamper-evidence (mirror T-0016 fully)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Duplicates the audit floor (T-0016) — §2/AC-21 fix that tamper-evidence of the governance act is the audit floor's job; the actor-event ledger is the typed SoD substrate. SoD reasons over content+order, not cryptographic tamper-evidence; append-only (privilege revoke + no-mutate trigger) already makes a submit/approve row un-rewritable without a CI-visible diff. Chaining would be gold-plating and would force a head table that AC-21 forbids.

rejected_alternatives.option: Model approve_L1..approve_Ln as N distinct verb strings in the CHECK set
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Unbounds the verb alphabet (approve_L1, approve_L2, ... approve_L7 — how many levels?) and re-couples 'add an approval level' to a CHECK migration. event='approve' + approve_level smallint keeps the verb set finite and closed (the GT-1-signed five) while making levels distinguishable AND orderable (L1<L2) numerically. The CHECK ((event='approve')=(approve_level IS NOT NULL)) ties them so a non-approve row can never smuggle a level and an approve row can never omit one.

rejected_alternatives.option: Open verb string (text, no CHECK) like audit_event.type
rejected_alternatives.why_not: audit_event.type is open because the audit floor records ANY governance event and a verifier reasons over the chain not the verb. SoD queries (T-0032) reason over a KNOWN FINITE verb alphabet; an open verb string would let an un-reviewed verb silently escape SoD coverage (an 'endorse' that is really an approve but is not checked). Closed-CHECK + vocab_version is the safe default GT-1 signed; extension stays possible but gated behind a reviewed migration.

rejected_alternatives.option: FK from role_at_event to a role table now
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The role table is undesigned (T-0022/E3.2). A baseline FK to a non-existent table fails to apply — the exact lesson of grant.role_id in 008_grant.sql, which carries a plain NOT NULL uuid with the FK deferred. role_at_event follows that precedent verbatim; AC-14 requires a non-existent role_at_event uuid to be ACCEPTED today; T-0022's migration adds (tenant_id,role_at_event)->role(tenant_id,id).

object_handle (T-0015, 009) fixed these as denormalized, non-FK nullable components: handles/records may be referenced before/without a hard FK and across the gateway, and a record-kind ref must be storable even if the record row is not yet present (opaque-pointer posture). AC-15 requires a record_id absent from `record` to be ACCEPTED. Enforcing the FK would couple the ledger to object lifecycle and break the gateway seam (FR-3/NF-4).

rejected_alternatives.option: Store a record/object payload or a denormalized snapshot column on actor_event
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates FR-6/NF-4 and mirrors the object_handle 'names fields, never values' invariant. A payload column would make the ledger a second object store and a second value-egress path bypassing the gateway (T-0021), the sole sanctioned value-resolver. The only jsonb permitted is detail (event metadata: a from->to state id, an approval-comment reference) which carries NO object field values.

rejected_alternatives.option: Add a kind column (human/agent) to actor_event to let SoD branch on it
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates FR-2/NF-3 — SoD treats a human and an agent as equal actors; an agent that submits then approves is a violation exactly as a human is. kind is resolvable by joining employee; making it a column of (or a discriminator in) actor_event would invite a SoD code-path that privileges one kind. AC-13 lints that no kind column exists and the ledger does not branch on employee.kind.

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.type: uuid NOT NULL no default; leading PK column; RLS key (T-0013 inheritance: FORCE RLS, default-DENY on choros.tenant_id GUC, withTenant)

fields.name: seq
fields.type: bigint NOT NULL; per-tenant STRICTLY-INCREASING (sparse-tolerant, NOT dense); UNIQUE(tenant_id,seq); PK is (tenant_id,seq) — the primary chronological access path

fields.name: id
fields.type: uuid NOT NULL; stable row identity; UNIQUE(tenant_id,id) so an audit_event row MAY reference it by uuid; NO FK between the ledgers (AC-21); generator = uuidv7 (time-ordered, so id roughly tracks seq; not load-bearing — order is seq)

fields.name: object_kind
fields.type: text NOT NULL; CHECK (object_kind IN ('application','registry','record')) — mirrors object_handle.ref_kind

fields.name: application_id
fields.type: uuid NULL; ResourceRef component, NO FK (T-0015 opaque-pointer pattern)

fields.name: registry_id
fields.type: uuid NULL; ResourceRef component, NO FK

fields.name: record_id
fields.type: uuid NULL; ResourceRef component, NO FK

fields.name: actor
fields.type: uuid NOT NULL; =performed_by (who physically performed); FK (tenant_id,actor)->employee(tenant_id,id), tenant-scoped both sides

fields.name: on_behalf_of
fields.type: uuid NULL; the principal when ≠ performer; FK (tenant_id,on_behalf_of)->employee(tenant_id,id); NULL ⇒ acted on own behalf; SoD principal = COALESCE(on_behalf_of,actor)

fields.name: role_at_event
fields.type: uuid NOT NULL; point-in-time role_id (the role the actor acted under at event-time, NOT current roles); NO FK (deferred to T-0022, mirrors grant.role_id)

fields.name: event
fields.type: text NOT NULL; CHECK (event IN ('request','prepare','submit','approve','release')) — closed verb set (§4.2)

fields.name: approve_level
fields.type: smallint NULL; the Ln of approve (>=1); CHECK ((event='approve') = (approve_level IS NOT NULL)) [non-null IFF approve] AND CHECK (approve_level IS NULL OR approve_level >= 1)

fields.name: detail
fields.type: jsonb NULL; verb-specific event metadata ONLY (e.g. from->to state id, approval-comment ref); NO object field values (FR-6)

fields.name: ts
fields.type: bigint NOT NULL; unix epoch ms wall-clock of the event; SoD ORDER reasoning uses seq NOT ts (clock skew)

fields.name: vocab_version
fields.type: smallint NOT NULL; pins the verb set + level semantics per row; verb-set change = CHECK edit + vocab bump (CI-visible)

fields.name: PRIMARY KEY
fields.type: (tenant_id, seq) — per-tenant order is the primary chronological access path; tenant_id leading (AC-3)

fields.name: UNIQUE (tenant_id, seq)
fields.type: subsumed by the PK; the per-tenant order/no-dup invariant (AC-8); a manual duplicate-seq insert is rejected

fields.name: UNIQUE (tenant_id, id)
fields.type: stable row identity so an audit_event row MAY reference it; NO FK (AC-21)

fields.name: INDEX object_read
fields.type: (tenant_id, object_kind, record_id, registry_id, application_id, seq) — object-scoped lookup is the PRIMARY read path (FR-3/AC-16: EXPLAIN shows index scan, ordered by seq within an object); tenant_id leading (AC-3)

fields.name: GRANT
fields.type: choros_app: SELECT, INSERT ONLY on actor_event (NO UPDATE/DELETE) — append-only privilege guard (FR-1a)

fields.name: no-mutate trigger
fields.type: BEFORE UPDATE + BEFORE DELETE on actor_event, function RAISEs restrict_violation for ALL roles incl. choros_migrator (FR-1b defence-in-depth; same shape as audit_event_immutable)

fields.name: RLS
fields.type: ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; one default-DENY policy USING/WITH CHECK tenant_id = current_setting('choros.tenant_id', true)::uuid (verbatim T-0013/audit_event pattern)

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.type: uuid NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY — exactly one counter row per tenant; RLS key (FORCE RLS, default-DENY, same as actor_event)

fields.name: next_seq
fields.type: bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1; the next seq to assign; advanced under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in the append path (per-tenant serialization, NO global lock/sequence)

fields.name: role_attrs
fields.type: this is NOT a head/chain artefact (no row_hash, no chain) — it is a bare per-tenant cursor, so AC-21 'no head table' holds; choros_app GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (it must advance next_seq); no DELETE

fields.name: first-append upsert
fields.type: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(tenant_id) DO NOTHING then SELECT FOR UPDATE (or upsert-then-lock); no pre-seeded counter required; genesis race -> one aborts on PK/serialization and retries (same retry posture as T-0016)

fields.name: verb_set
fields.type: {request, prepare, submit, approve, release} — the GT-1-signed closed set; pinned as the CHECK on event; changing it = CHECK edit + vocab bump (golden test fails CI otherwise, AC-20)

fields.name: level_semantics
fields.type: approve carries approve_level smallint >= 1; L1<L2<.. orderable; non-approve verbs carry NULL level (CHECK-tied)

fields.name: actor_event_grants
fields.type: SELECT, INSERT ONLY (NO UPDATE, NO DELETE) — FR-1a append-only privilege guard

fields.name: actor_event_seq_grants
fields.type: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (NO DELETE) — the counter must advance; no delete of a tenant's cursor

fields.name: role_attrs
fields.type: NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, not table owner (T-0013)

fields.name: ownership
fields.type: owns actor_event + actor_event_seq; holds DDL; never used at runtime

fields.name: cannot_mutate_actor_event
fields.type: even the owner cannot UPDATE/DELETE actor_event — the no-mutate trigger fires regardless of role (AC-6); only a CI-visible DISABLE/DROP TRIGGER diff lifts it

contracts: appendActorEvent(tx, e: ActorEventInput): { seq, id } — the ONLY sanctioned writer (FR-7), called by the guarded-transition/gateway path (T-0021/E4.2) at ACTION-TIME, inside withTenant (T-0013). Steps: (1) per-tenant serialization for the ordinal — INSERT INTO actor_event_seq(tenant_id,next_seq) VALUES (TENANT,1) ON CONFLICT(tenant_id) DO NOTHING; then SELECT next_seq FROM actor_event_seq WHERE tenant_id=GUC FOR UPDATE; seq := next_seq; UPDATE actor_event_seq SET next_seq = next_seq + 1 WHERE tenant_id=GUC (per-tenant, race-free, NO global lock/sequence — NF-2). (2) id := uuidv7(). (3) INSERT ONE row into actor_event (tenant_id,seq,id, object_kind/application_id/registry_id/record_id from e, actor=e.actor, on_behalf_of=e.onBehalfOf ?? NULL, role_at_event=e.roleAtEvent, event=e.event, approve_level = e.event='approve' ? e.approveLevel : NULL, detail=e.detail ?? NULL, ts=now_ms(), vocab_version=VOCAB). Append-only: INSERT only, NEVER a read-modify-write of prior rows. RETRY: on the genesis seq race (two appends both compute seq=1) one aborts on UNIQUE(tenant_id,seq)/serialization and MUST re-run from step 1 (re-read next_seq under FOR UPDATE); a stale seq is never reused.

ActorEventInput (TS mirror, camelCase; uuid->string, bigint epoch-ms->number; T-0014/T-0017 convention): { objectKind: 'application'|'registry'|'record'; applicationId?: string; registryId?: string; recordId?: string; actor: string; onBehalfOf?: string|null; roleAtEvent: string; event: 'request'|'prepare'|'submit'|'approve'|'release'; approveLevel?: number; detail?: Record<string,unknown>|null }. Validation: approveLevel required IFF event==='approve' and >=1; exactly the object-component(s) implied by objectKind populated (record->recordId, registry->registryId, application->applicationId).

READ contract (SoD substrate, consumed by T-0032/E4.2 — T-0019 freezes the shapes, NOT the SoD constraints). All run under the actor's tenant RLS context (withTenant). (a) per-object ordered trail: SELECT * FROM actor_event WHERE tenant_id=GUC AND object_kind=$k AND <component_id>=$id ORDER BY seq (index-served via the object_read index). (b) dynamic-SoD substrate 'did principal P perform event E on object X?': SELECT EXISTS(... WHERE <object predicate> AND event=$E AND COALESCE(on_behalf_of, actor)=$P) — delegated acts attribute to the principal, self-acts (on_behalf_of NULL) to actor. (c) static-SoD substrate 'which roles acted on object X?': SELECT DISTINCT role_at_event FROM actor_event WHERE <object predicate> [AND event = ANY($events)]. These are read shapes; sod_constraint evaluation + the action-time block are T-0032/E4.2.

Ledger boundary contract (§2/AC-22): a guarded transition writes ONE actor_event row (the SoD fact) AND ONE audit_event row (the tamper-evident fact) in distinct tables. The audit_event row MAY carry the actor_event.id (a uuid) in its payload/scope to cross-reference, but there is NO enforced FK between actor_event and audit_event — each is independently append-only. T-0019 does NOT couple the two writes (that is the writer's design, T-0021/E4.2); it only fixes that both rows exist, are distinct, and neither subsumes the other (no chain/head on actor_event).

Structural enforcement (migration 018 SQL, built by coder): (A) GRANT SELECT,INSERT ON actor_event TO choros_app (NO UPDATE/DELETE) + GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE ON actor_event_seq TO choros_app (NO DELETE). (B) CREATE FUNCTION actor_event_immutable() RAISE EXCEPTION restrict_violation + BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers on actor_event firing for ALL roles. (A)+(B) held SIMULTANEOUSLY — defeating append-only needs a CI-visible diff that BOTH grants the privilege AND drops/disables the trigger. (C) the closed verb CHECK, the approve_level IFF CHECK, the object_kind CHECK, and the FORCE-RLS default-DENY policy are all DDL constraints (not runtime guards).
